title: I Used the Orchid-House Mister Hours on the Chair Who Camped the Bench

parts.text: I booked mister bay 2 at 7:14 a.m. and chair Ines was already camped on the only tagged bench. The card said: BOOK THE BAY. FORTY MINUTES. BENCH WITH THE TAG. I was forty-four, volunteer, holding a tag. Ines shrugged. "Chairs are the house." I photographed the card, the tag, and her bags on the bench. Then I asked for the mister log. At 7:20 horticulture pinged why Ines's name was on a camped bench. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Horticulture can see Ines's bags on the tagged bench during my mister hours.

social.video_title: The chair camped the only tagged orchid bench — Part 1/2
social.description: Orchid house, a forty-minute bay, bags on the tag. I logged the camp. Would you have asked horticulture?

parts.text: Ines called it stewardship until horticulture asked for the still. I printed the log, the card, and the photo. The bags moved. Ines booked her own forty and told the next chair stewardship was always about optics. Optics is a word chairs use when misters exist. Hours now have a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE BENCH. I keep bay 2. Ines brown-bags the jokes. The house finally looks like a tag, not a camp. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Chairs are not the bench — Part 2/2
social.description: Mister log, moved bags, and a second line. Was stewardship ever my tag?
